title: When can a lithium-ion cell design search trust a reduced battery model (SPMe) instead of the full DFN model?
lede: research programme on fidelity-aware Li-ion electrode design; milestone 1: SPMe's own minimum electrolyte concentration from a 2-cycle run flags the designs it mis-scores by over 25% with ROC AUC 0.997 (7 of 49), but a 2-cycle DFN run costs about the same as the SPMe one (1.3 s against 1.2 s) and the cost is in the cycle count (100-cycle DFN 27.9 s), so short-horizon DFN may beat reduced physics as the cheap screen (modelled, PyBaMM OKane2022, stack level)
summary: A research programme (proposal and log on the project page) on when a lithium-ion electrode design search can trust a reduced electrochemical model. Milestone 1 uses the 49 designs of energy-cell-dfn with their committed 100-cycle SPMe and DFN scores: a 2-cycle SPMe run's minimum electrolyte concentration, divided by the initial value, classifies the 7 designs SPMe under-scores by more than 25% with ROC AUC 0.997 (bootstrap 95% 0.980–1.000; 0.994 over the designs SPMe solved), and its Spearman correlation with the score gap is −0.83. Three designs reach a negative salt concentration under SPMe. The pre-registered cost hypothesis failed: a 2-cycle run costs 1.2 s under SPMe and 1.3 s under DFN, while 100 cycles cost 3.9 s and 27.9 s, so reducing the cycle count saves 21× on DFN against 7× for swapping in SPMe. A replay shows DFN on the top 10 SPMe designs finds the DFN best of the 49. Limits: one parameter set and protocol, a stratified sample with 7 positives, timings from one machine, no measured cell for these designs.
